source.title: Towards Consistent Geospatial Representations: Aligning One Encoder to Many Foundation Models

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, but the similarity figures are represented by captions rather than their plotted values; only similarity results stated in the text can be recorded.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures similarity between geospatial foundation-model embeddings using CCA, CKA, and standardized CKA, but does not test the claim’s scale trend. This is a conceptual test of representation similarity in a new setting.
record.gate_note: The paper measures pairwise embedding similarity and complementarity for five geospatial foundation models across 11 datasets. It does not sweep model size or capability. The student encoder is deliberately trained to align to teacher embeddings, so that alignment is not evidence of naturally arising convergence. Most plotted pairwise results are not available in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study measures pairwise standardized CKA among five independently trained geospatial foundation models (GFMs) on 11 datasets. It reports partial, dataset-dependent similarity, a new setting with results bearing on V7 (partial convergence) and V6 (data dependence). There is no scale sweep, so it does not test V1. The GeoMixture student is aligned to its teachers on purpose, so it does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find GFM embeddings partially similar and complementary, with both depending on the dataset, and similarity not predicting complementarity. GeoMixture ties the best GFM in average rank and is more consistent across datasets. The stated limitation is that alignment is done per dataset on unlabeled target imagery, so the results measure specialization rather than transfer. Evaluation covers 9 of 11 datasets, and the loss is ablated on 5.
record.recipe_differences: Measures pairwise CCA, CKA, and standardized CKA among geospatial foundation-model embeddings and reports complementarity; it does not test representation similarity as a function of model scale or performance.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported standardized-CKA similarity and complementarity vary by dataset. The authors state that CCA and linear CKA have limitations and therefore use standardized CKA for the main similarity analysis; plotted metric-by-metric results are not available in the supplied text.

fits_no_version.finding: Representation similarity does not reliably predict whether concatenating two GFM embeddings improves a downstream probe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pairwise similarity of foundation-model embeddings is not a reliable predictor of their downstream complementarity.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: 2nd Workshop on Advances in Representation Learning for Earth Observation
record.problems: No scale or capability sweep is performed. The similarity analysis covers five GFMs and is dataset-specific; similarity uncertainty is not reported in the text. The complementarity score can overfit high-dimensional latents, is sensitive to regularization, and can collapse to the majority class on imbalanced datasets. The student is aligned per dataset using unlabeled target imagery, limiting transfer conclusions. The supplied text includes figure captions but not the plotted pairwise values.
record.rows_left_out: The paper presents CCA, CKA, standardized-CKA and complementarity plots for all 11 datasets in Figures 2–13, but most plotted values are not present in the supplied text and are not individually extractable. The reported explicit numerical examples and the stated qualitative relationship are retained.

untested.parts: No model size or capability sweep; no test of whether alignment rises with scale.
No mapping between independently trained models is evaluated. The student is trained deliberately to match its teachers.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
No numeric CCA vs CKA vs standardized CKA comparison is in the text (plots only). No neighbour-count or out-of-distribution tests.
Plateauing and the causes of alignment (shared data or objectives) are not tested.

missing.what: Explicit statement that similarity scores vary by dataset, plus per-dataset standardized CKA values for each pair. Needed for a proper V6 row; currently only in plots.
CCA and linear CKA values alongside standardized CKA, which would show metric dependence. The authors argue CKA is dominated by high-variance directions in GFM features.

record.verdict_notes: The models compared differ in objective, modality and partly in architecture, but they share remote-sensing pretraining domains; shared data as a cause is not examined. Similarity uncertainty is not reported. The tranche is changed from T2 to T3 because this is a new domain, not a new method for the original question.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no test of whether alignment rises with scale or performance.
No comparison across random initialization seeds of the same architecture.
The deliberately aligned student is evaluated for downstream performance, not for whether one independently trained model’s representations can be mapped to another’s with little loss.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Dataset dependence is explicitly reported. The text does not provide plotted values sufficient to compare results across CCA, CKA, and standardized CKA, and it does not test other settings such as neighbour count or out-of-distribution inputs.
The study reports partial similarity and dataset-dependent results, but does not test whether similarity plateaus or whether shared pretraining data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: Scale-MAE × DOFA embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise standardized CKA between frozen GFM embeddings and averaged the result over the 11 PANGAEA-LATENTS datasets.
rows.locator: Section 4, Fig. 2; similarity and complementarity discussion
rows.note: The paper describes this pair as dissimilar. The value is an aggregate over datasets, not a scale comparison.
rows.check: V7 predicts partial alignment, and a standardized CKA of 0.26 is that partial alignment, so the state is observed, not partial. A single aggregate value cannot show metric or data dependence, so the V6 link is removed.

rows.subject: CROMA × TerraMind-L embeddings
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise standardized CKA between frozen GFM embeddings and averaged the result over the 11 PANGAEA-LATENTS datasets.
rows.locator: Section 4, Fig. 2; similarity and complementarity discussion
rows.note: The paper describes this pair as highly similar. The value is an aggregate over datasets, not a scale comparison.
rows.check: 0.83 is the most similar pair but still not complete alignment, which is what V7 describes, so the state is observed. Its V6 relevance comes only from comparison with r4 (same pair, 0.77 on CropTypeMapping), which the verdict cites; a lone aggregate value cannot carry V6.

rows.note: The paper uses this as an example of a dissimilar pair.
rows.check: Partial similarity (0.17) is consistent with V7, so the state is observed. A single-dataset value cannot by itself show dataset dependence.

relationships.condition: 5 GFMs with differing objectives and modalities, standardized CKA on PANGAEA-LATENTS
relationships.reason: Pairwise similarity ranges from 0.17 to 0.83, never near complete; the authors call the embeddings 'neither redundant nor disjoint' (r1–r5).
relationships.display_finding: Standardized pairwise CKA ranged from 0.17 to 0.83, indicating representations that were neither redundant nor disjoint.

relationships.condition: Choice of input dataset among 11 PANGAEA datasets
relationships.reason: The text states similarity scores 'depend on the dataset'. The numeric evidence is only modest: CROMA×TerraMind-L is 0.83 averaged vs 0.77 on CropTypeMapping (r2, r4). The verdict rests mainly on the text.
relationships.display_finding: CROMA–TerraMind-L similarity was 0.83 averaged across datasets versus 0.77 on CropTypeMapping, consistent with the reported dataset dependence.
